investigation.title: Remote Agent Provisioning: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocking All Remote-Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-10-10T12:35:48Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error indicating the swarm gateway ELB endpoint at /v1/agents was unreachable during agent provisioning. Because the failure occurs at the very first network call to the swarm gateway — before any agent identity, VM ID, or state can be returned — all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent and every contract assertion is unverifiable.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm gateway (an AWS ELB in us-east-2 fronting /v1/agents) was unreachable at the time of the eval run. The production-api layer received a 502 bad_gateway when attempting to POST to the swarm gateway during remote agent provisioning. Because this is the shared upstream dependency for all three remote-agent checks, all checks failed with the same error message and produced empty evidence objects. This is an eval-observed infrastructure connectivity failure localized to the swarm gateway endpoint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact to production end-users cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.

investigations.summary: The eval for the published-observability-snapshot check failed because the snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json was 686 minutes old at eval time, more than double the 300-minute maximum asserted by the expected-output contract. All other public-website sibling checks passed, isolating the failure entirely to the staleness of the published snapshot JSON, not to the website's reachability or any shared infrastructure dependency.
investigations.rootCause: The GitHub Actions workflow responsible for regenerating and publishing the observability snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json did not run successfully within the required 300-minute window. The snapshot was last written approximately 686 minutes before the eval ran (2026-10-10T12:36:24Z), meaning the workflow that produces and publishes the snapshot file either failed, was skipped, was cancelled, or was not scheduled to run for at least the preceding ~6.4 hours. This is an eval-layer signal about a stale published artifact; no evidence of a user-facing outage or traffic disruption is present in the packet.

The GitHub Pages deployment step succeeded in triggering but the CDN or Pages cache served a stale version of status.json, causing the age computed from the file's embedded timestamp to appear older than the actual workflow run time.
A transient GitHub Actions outage or queue delay caused the scheduled run to be delayed beyond the 300-minute threshold without a failure notification.
